messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Poète j'étais et chantai ce juste fils d'Anchise qui vint de Troie, après que le fier Ilion fut brûlé.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Alignment Table (Italian → French)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-------------------------------------------|----------------------|-----------------------|--------| | Poeta | speaker’s identity as a poet | Poète | poet | OK | | fui | copular past “was” (identity) | j’étais | I was | OK | | e | coordinating conjunction linking clauses | et | and | OK | | cantai | performed singing (past) | chantai | sang | OK | | di *(line 73)* | preposition “of” introducing object of singing | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | quel | demonstrative determiner specifying “just” | ce | that/this | OK | | giusto | property “just” ascribed to the referent | juste | just | OK | | figliuol | male offspring of Anchises | fils | son | OK | | d'Anchise | genitive relation “of Anchises” | d'Anchise | of Anchises | OK | | che *(line 74)* | relative pronoun introducing clause about the son | qui | who | OK | | venne | motion event “came” from Troy | vint | came | OK | | di *(line 74)* | preposition “from” indicating origin | de | from | OK | | Troia | city of origin | Troie | Troy | OK | | poi | temporal adverb “after” | après | after | OK | | che *(line 75)* | subordinating conjunction linking result clause | que | that (introducing result) | OK | | 'l | definite article for Ilion | le | the | OK | | superbo | attribute “proud” describing Ilion | fier | proud | OK | | Ilïón | city that was burned | Ilion | Ilion | OK | | fu | auxiliary forming passive perfect “was” | fut | was (aux) | OK | | combusto | passive participle “burned” | brûlé | burned | OK |
### Items flagged - **UNNECESSARY**: *di* (line 73) – the preposition “of” is not required in French; the demonstrative *ce* already conveys the reference.
No other tokens are missing, wrong, or grammatically problematic.
